pain_points.section: §2 Step types at a glance / §7 Worked example
pain_points.description: The `ai` step example in §7 includes `agent: claude` and `model: sonnet`, but the §2 table lists only `prompt` and `contract` as required keys for `ai`. The guide never says whether `agent`/`model` are required, recommended, or optional with defaults — I had to guess they were safe to include by copying the worked example.

In §7 the write-file step takes `--output-path $inputs.output_path` and *also* declares `output_path` in its contract — implying the script both consumes a caller-supplied path and emits one. The scenario gives a fixed target (~/.harness/artifacts/<run-id>/notes.md) so I dropped the input but kept the contract field. The guide doesn't explicitly cover the 'script computes its own path from run_id' pattern, so I had to infer.

The guide shows `$inputs.X` and `$state.X` substitution inside YAML scalars (e.g. args lists). It's not 100% explicit that the same substitution happens inside `template_vars` string values (vs. requiring Jinja-style {{ inputs.x }} there). §7's `subject:` field uses `$inputs.since_days` and `$state.tickets` as substitution tokens inside the string, which I copied — but a one-line note 'template_vars strings get $-substitution before Jinja render' would remove the ambiguity.
summarize.j2's header lists `length` as optional and `subject` as required, but the guide table in §5 only lists required vars. Having the optional ones surfaced in §5 would save a file read.
The four primitive types are listed as `string, integer, boolean, number` — but earlier the sentence says 'Three primitive types' then names four. Cosmetic but it made me re-read.

The write-file script in §7 takes `--output-path` as a flag but also writes `output_path` to state via contract — slightly circular. For my scenario where the path is fully derived from run_id, I passed the rendered markdown via --content; the guide doesn't show how scripts typically receive large state values (flag vs stdin vs reading state file). Guessed --content flag.

self_assessment: I believe the workflow loads. Required workflow-level fields (name, version, steps) are present; each step has id/type/contract/writes with names matching contract field names exactly; the AI step uses prompts/standard/summarize.j2 with its required `subject` template var; no worktree/loop/decision used as the scenario specifies a 3-stage informational workflow. The one area I'm least certain about is whether `agent`/`model` on the ai step are required defaults — I included them mirroring §7.
